name: Dakshina dataset v1.0 (Google Research), Malayalam
licence_source: https://github.com/google-research-datasets/dakshina/blob/master/README.md#license ("The dataset is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0"). The repo has no LICENSE file.
attribution: Dakshina dataset by Google Research (Roark et al., 2020, LREC), CC BY-SA 4.0. Native-script text from Wikipedia; romanisations by Google's annotators.
verdict_reason: Share-alike, same position as Wikipedia (see the licence audit). Human romanisations are exactly what the rule probabilities need. Train split for training and for fitting the rule probabilities; dev and test splits held out for eval.
used_for: Only ml/lexicons/ml.translit.sampled.{train,dev,test}.tsv (native word, romanisation, annotator count). Train: transliterator training pairs and the romaniser's rule calibration (training/mlkb/data/calibrate.py). Dev: validation during training. Test: data/eval/translit-human.tsv (2,000 pairs). Dev and test words are kept out of every training pair. The romanized/ sentences and the native_script_wikipedia text (a copy of mlwiki) aren't used.
notes: The tar holds all 12 languages (2,008,340,480 bytes). After data/fetch.sh, extract only the Malayalam lexicons: tar -xf data/raw/dakshina/dakshina_dataset_v1.0.tar -C data/raw/dakshina 'dakshina_dataset_v1.0/ml/lexicons/*'. The SHA-256 of each extracted file is under `extracted`.
